items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: It was Bill Price on trumpet and Alan Fredrickson on trombone and myself. And there was a piano player named Paul Jackson and a banjo player named Paul Boeberg and Jack Seldon on drums.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Jack Selden was from Texas, is that right? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I remember him going back and I corresponded with him years later, but I hadn't heard of him in recent years. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. That is maybe in mid-50s or something. I don't know if we had an exchange or two. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now in 49, you came to, 48 rather, you came to the University. And do you remember who made up the first groups that you played with? Was it then called the…

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, it didn't have a name at first. We just sort of thought that was a hot sounding name, so we adopted it. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It was Bill Price on trumpet and Alan Fredrickson on trombone and myself. And there was a piano player named Paul Jackson and a banjo player named Paul Boeberg and Jack Seldon on drums. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I think that was the regular group. There may have been others who played from time to time.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Then about the time you left, some of the others left too, that is the band more or less broke up about 50, didn't it? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Bill Price kept a group together, but your group had pretty well spread.
